walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordinate Systems & Time — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordinate Systems & Time brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordinate Systems & Time.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the full MK class of the Sun?
options: G0V
G2V
K5III
M0V

mcqs.q: Class V denotes which type of star?
options: Supergiant
Giant
Main sequence
White dwarf

mcqs.q: Why are Type Ia supernovae used as 'standard candles'?
options: Because they happen at regular time intervals.
Where humans could survive without spacesuits.
They have nearly uniform peak brightness, so their apparent brightness reveals distance.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.

mcqs.q: What is the 'habitable zone' around a star?
options: Where humans could survive without spacesuits.
Where life definitely exists.
On the outermost edge.
The region where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface.

mcqs.q: Where is our Solar System located in the Milky Way?
options: About two-thirds of the way out from the centre, in one of the spiral arms.
Right at the centre of the galaxy.
On the outermost edge.
Where humans could survive without spacesuits.
